name: Nahum

overview.author: Nahum the Elkoshite (1:1), whose name means “comfort.”
overview.date: Between the fall of Thebes (663 BC, mentioned in 3:8) and the fall of Nineveh (612 BC).
overview.audience: Judah, which had suffered under Assyrian domination.
overview.setting: Assyria, once spared after Jonah’s preaching, had returned to cruelty, destroyed Israel, and oppressed Judah. Its capital, Nineveh, seemed invincible.
overview.purpose: To announce the certain destruction of Nineveh and comfort Judah with God’s justice and protection.
overview.structure: God’s character as avenger and refuge (1), the vivid fall of Nineveh (2), and the reasons for Nineveh’s doom (3).

items.title: Judgment on Nineveh, good news for Judah

themes.title: God’s Justice
themes.text: “The LORD will by no means clear the guilty” (1:3).

themes.title: God’s Goodness
themes.text: “The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble” (1:7).

themes.title: God’s Patience Has Limits
themes.text: Nineveh’s earlier repentance under Jonah did not last.

themes.title: Comfort for the Oppressed
themes.text: The fall of the oppressor is good news for God’s people.

themes.title: God Opposes the Proud and Violent

keyVerses.quote: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, and the LORD will by no means clear the guilty.
The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; he knows those who take refuge in him.
Behold, upon the mountains, the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace!

christInBook.text: The herald bringing good news of peace points to the gospel of Christ (Isaiah 52:7; Romans 10:15).
Christ is the stronghold for those who take refuge in Him from the coming wrath (1 Thessalonians 1:10).
God’s wrath against sin is satisfied at the cross for those who believe (Romans 3:25–26).

crossReferences.note: Feet of those who bring good news.
The fall of Babylon the great.

reflection: How do Nahum 1:3 and 1:7 together give a balanced view of God?
How does knowing God will judge oppressors comfort you?
How does Nineveh’s story warn against shallow or temporary repentance?
Where do you need God to be your stronghold today?
Who needs to hear the good news of peace from you (1:15)?

chapterList.title: The LORD Is Avenging and Good
chapterList.summary: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God, slow to anger but great in power, who will not clear the guilty. Mountains quake before Him. Yet “the LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble.” He will make an end of Nineveh and break Judah’s yoke. A messenger brings good news of peace.
questions: How can God be both avenging (1:2) and good (1:7)?
What does it mean that God “knows those who take refuge in him”?
How does Paul use the image of 1:15 (Romans 10:15)?

chapterList.title: Nineveh Falls
chapterList.summary: A vivid scene: the attacker advances, chariots race through the streets, the river gates open, and the palace melts. Nineveh, once a lion’s den full of prey, is plundered. “Behold, I am against you, declares the LORD of hosts.”
questions: What details make this description so vivid?
What does the lion’s den image say about Assyria (2:11–12)?
How should “I am against you” (2:13) warn every proud power?

chapterList.title: Woe to the Bloody City
chapterList.summary: “Woe to the bloody city, all full of lies and plunder.” Nineveh’s prostitution and sorceries brought judgment. Like Thebes, it will fall. Its defenses are like ripe figs, its merchants like locusts. “All who hear the news about you clap their hands over you. For upon whom has not come your unceasing evil?”
questions: What sins does God name in 3:1–4?
What does the final verse say about Nineveh’s cruelty?

tagline: The fall of Nineveh: the LORD is slow to anger but will by no means clear the guilty
readingPlan: 3 chapters: one chapter a day takes 3 days; two a day takes about 2 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
